articles.title: Culture experiment on microbial indole production
articles.abstract: In this fictional experiment, isolated bacteria were cultured with labeled tryptophan. Investigators measured labeled indole appearing in the culture medium and compared an enzyme deletion strain with a restored strain.

articles.title: Indole exposure and bacterial survival
articles.abstract: This fictional study added manufactured indole to bacterial cultures and counted surviving bacteria. It did not measure bacterial conversion of tryptophan or production of indole.

articles.title: Direct binding of a ligand to a purified receptor
articles.abstract: This fictional cell-free experiment measured concentration-dependent binding of a labeled ligand to purified receptor protein. Unlabeled competitor displaced the ligand, and a saturation curve was recorded.

articles.title: Receptor gene expression after ligand treatment
articles.abstract: This fictional cell experiment measured receptor messenger RNA after ligand exposure. Receptor abundance changed. No purified protein, displacement assay, or direct ligand binding measurement was used.

articles.title: Stable isotope tracing of metabolic pathway flux
articles.abstract: This fictional study supplied labeled carbon substrate, collected a time series of downstream isotope enrichment, and estimated the rate of material passing through a metabolic pathway with a specified kinetic model.

articles.title: Metabolite concentrations in a single blood sample
articles.abstract: This fictional study measured unlabeled metabolite pool sizes once in each sample. The authors discussed pathway flux but collected no isotope tracing, time series, or rate measurements.

articles.title: Randomized stress challenge with autonomic measurements
articles.abstract: This fictional within-person experiment randomly ordered a stress task and a neutral control task. Heart rate and skin conductance were measured repeatedly before and after each task.

articles.title: Cross-sectional questionnaire about stress and heart rate
articles.abstract: This fictional survey recorded self-reported stress and resting heart rate once. Participants were not assigned to a stress challenge or control condition, and no repeated autonomic measurements were collected.
